meta.title: mtmux privacy policy — what we collect and why
meta.description: mtmux never sees your terminal contents. See what metadata we collect, what we never touch, our third parties, and how to export or delete your data.

paragraphs.p1: We never see your terminal contents. When traffic is relayed through our servers it is encrypted end-to-end between your machine and your browser, under keys derived on those two devices, and we forward ciphertext we cannot read. When your devices reach each other directly — on your own network, or over the internet without our relay — that connection does not pass through us at all, and it is protected by the browser’s own transport security rather than by us. Either way, we do not store your terminal contents. Everything below is detail on the small amount of metadata that makes the service work — and if you run mtmux in local mode, none of it exists, because your machine never contacts us at all.

i1.text: only if you create an account: your email, and a customer identifier from our payment processor if you subscribe. Card details never touch our servers.

i2.text: connection timestamps, device identifiers, byte counts and outcome codes — enough to enforce plan limits and debug a failed pairing. Not the contents of anything.

i3.text: aggregate page counts with no cookies, no cross-site identifiers and no ad networks.

i1.text: Terminal output, keystrokes, file contents, paths or environment variables.

i2.text: Your source code, in any form, at any time.

i3.text: The secret half of a pairing code — it is never transmitted, not even as a hash.

i4.text: SSH keys. mtmux never asks for one and has nowhere to put one.

i5.text: Anything at all from a machine running in local mode.

paragraphs.p1: Dodo Payments handles subscriptions and is the merchant of record; card details go to them and never to us. Beyond that, a hosting provider runs the broker. There is no analytics vendor, no ad network, no notification provider and no chat widget.
paragraphs.p2: mtmux does not send notifications, so nothing is routed to Slack, Apple, Google or any other messaging service on your behalf.

paragraphs.p1: Session frames are never written to disk by the broker — they are relayed and discarded. Connection metadata is kept only as long as it is useful for abuse prevention and debugging, and account data for as long as you have an account. Delete the account and it goes with it.
Email <email>privacy@mtmux.com</email> to export or delete everything associated with your account; we complete requests within 30 days. Self-hosted installs hold their own data, and we never see it.
Material changes are announced in the <changelogLink>changelog</changelogLink> and by email to account holders before taking effect.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.lastUpdated: Not legal advice; this is the agreement itself.

paragraphs.p1: mtmux provides a command-line program, a browser client and an optional hosted pairing broker. Using the hosted broker means accepting these terms. If you only use local mode, or run the broker yourself, no part of the service is involved and only section 2 applies.

The mtmux CLI is published under the MIT licence, as stated in its package metadata, and the browser client ships with it. Nothing here narrows that licence: the MIT terms govern the software, and these terms govern the hosted service.

i1.text: You are responsible for what runs in your sessions and for which browsers you pair. A paired browser can drive your terminal — treat pairing as seriously as handing over a shell.

i2.text: Do not use mtmux to access systems you are not authorised to access, or in violation of your employer's policy.

i3.text: Do not use the broker for bulk data transfer, general-purpose port forwarding, cryptomining, or anything that degrades it for other people.

paragraphs.p1: Subscriptions are processed by Dodo Payments and renew until cancelled. Cancel any time and keep paid features until the period ends. Refunds are given on request within 30 days of a charge. Prices may change with notice; your current period is never repriced.

The hosted broker is provided as-is, with no uptime commitment and no service level agreement. We do not offer one because we are not yet in a position to honour one, and a number we could not stand behind would be worse than none. If uninterrupted access matters to you, use local mode or run the broker yourself — both are supported and neither depends on us.

You may stop using mtmux at any time; <cmd>mtmux stop</cmd> ends the server on a machine and <cmd>mtmux devices revoke</cmd> ends a browser's access. We may suspend accounts that abuse the broker or violate section 3, with notice where practical.

The software is provided as-is. To the extent permitted by law, our aggregate liability is limited to the amount you paid in the preceding 12 months. We are not liable for lost work, or for actions taken by programs — including coding agents — running in your sessions.
Questions about these terms: <email>hey@mtmux.com</email>. Security reports: <email>security@mtmux.com</email>.
